promptLatex: A class has 30 students. 18 like algebra, 15 like geometry, and 10 like both algebra and geometry. How many students like neither algebra nor geometry?
hintLatex:
Use inclusion-exclusion for two sets.
|A ∪ G| = |A| + |G| - |A ∩ G| = 18 + 15 - 10 = 23.
Students who like neither: 30 - 23 = 7.

The number of students who like at least one of algebra or geometry is 23.
The number who like neither is 30 - 23 = 7.
solutionLatex:
Use the inclusion-exclusion principle for two sets A (algebra) and G (geometry).

|A ∪ G| = |A| + |G| - |A ∩ G| = 18 + 15 - 10 = 23.

This is the number of students who like algebra or geometry (or both).

Students who like neither: 30 - 23 = 7.
